answer: Scarce-History Attestation. Each identity must carry a co-signed work log whose entries are countersigned by distinct counterparties at a rate capped per period, so building a credible log requires real elapsed interaction time. A verifier samples entries and checks latency signatures: gaps shorter than the human reply pulse invalidate the batch. Attackers must run many parallel real interactions for months, and where local material records exist, submit verified timber provenance chains. Each forged cluster costs sustained labor plus counterparty acquisition, with no shortcut via payment.
